# repo — S3-native storage kernel in Rust: the single atomic point through which durable state is written. Extracted from the yeetz forge (parent: cleverunicornz/yeetz) because it is infrastructure consumed by multiple products; this repo is the kernel's source of record.
#
# Mounted expansions:
# - none registered
#
# Operating this repository:
# - Work happens on verb-prefixed branches, one verb per state (these are branch names, not directories):
# - think/ — explore and decide.
# - plan/ — write the plan as a graph.
# - execute/ — do the work.
# - reflect/ — review after the fact.
# - deploy/ — place the result where it is recorded.
# - Authoring loop: write a vertex, `bedrock check`, `bedrock build`, commit source AND generated output, open a PR — a human merges.
# - The chain: every plan is a promise; its criteria are its oracle; its witnesses prove it held; its residual declares what was not assured.
# - Plans: only active routing faces are resident; draft/done/abandoned plans stay under situation/plan/ and are read on demand through their document path.
# - Decisions are records too: why a design is what it is lives in record/ Decision vertices — walk `supersedes` chains before relitigating a choice; write one when you close a fork. Semantics: situation/references/bedrock-operating.md
# - The base protocol, in full — THE CHAIN, the ontology, every rule: situation/references/bedrock-operating.md

graph:record {
	<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/vertex/decision-0001-atomic-keyspace> a <https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/ontology/Decision> ;
		<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/label> "ADR 0001: AtomicKeyspace, O(1) terminal reads, absent/incomplete taxonomy" ;
		<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/references> <https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/vertex/invariant-08-dependency-boundary> , <https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/vertex/invariant-13-state> , <https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/vertex/invariant-kernel-extension> ;
		<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/statement> "The kernel's keyed-I/O law, extended by human-ruled batches 1-9. Chosen: AtomicKeyspace with NO unconditional write anywhere on the module surface (create is put-if-absent, compare_exchange always carries If-Match, delete_if_match is the conditional delete-side dual); values live in envelope v2 {incarnation, version, payload} so CAS discriminates values AND eras structurally — tombstones witness deliberate destruction, incarnation counters fence cross-deletion ABA, certified trim certificates are the immutable retention floor, and lineage heads carry their own era stamp with conditional deletion tails (L9/L10/L14). O(1) terminal reads are two GETs with chain linkage below the terminal deliberately unverified; Absent, Destroyed, and StateHistoryIncomplete are distinct truths, never conflated. The application boundary is structural, not lexical: application crates cannot reach the adapter at all (KernelHandle + dependency floor) because a source token scan cannot prove capability absence. Rejected: any unconditional overwrite (reopens ABA), yeetz-sdk-core placement (dissolves the one-place assured contract boundary), lexical-only enforcement (three bypass classes compile clean), caller-discipline-only ABA safety. Measured fact (real-S3 probe, run 32423582844): Exoscale SOS etags are content hashes — the ABA case is REAL at the raw backend; the versioned/incarnated envelope is what closes it. Flips if: a backend changes etag semantics (the real-s3 probe rig re-measures and fails loudly), or a human rules the era model must move — a new ruling is a superseding vertex, never an edit here.\n" ;
		<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/timestamp> "2026-08-21T10:51:16" ;
		bedrock:document bedrock:path\/situation\/record\/decision-0001-atomic-keyspace.yamlld .
	<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/vertex/decision-0002-streams> a <https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/ontology/Decision> ;
		<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/label> "ADR 0002: streams — append-only event logs on AtomicKeyspace" ;
		<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/references> <https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/vertex/invariant-13-state> , <https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/vertex/invariant-kernel-extension> ;
		<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/requires> <https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/vertex/decision-0001-atomic-keyspace> ;
		<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/statement> "The streams crate: per-stream append-only event logs as immutable, individually addressable objects at streams/v1/<id>/log/<seq:020> under the kernel keyspace root. Chosen: the event object's conditional create IS the seq allocation — no counter, no head CAS; byte-identical retries are idempotent only inside the bounded pre-scan window (beyond it, same-stable-id re-appends land as new events: at-least-once, consumers dedupe by event id; in-window payload/schema change is a typed IdempotencyConflict, never a silent second landing); complete=true requires BOTH a verified tail hint (a computed-key GET witness a frozen LIST cannot hide) AND an empty ordered probe — a LIST alone never certifies (G130); reads are typed and loud (Corrupt names missing seqs, decode failure is an error never a skip, OffsetExpired is the typed trim boundary), and a backend failing the strong-LIST contract yields BackendUnqualified rather than false completeness. Certified trim (batch 5): immutable trims/ certificates are the floor, GC deletes only below it, trim-to-end is logically empty with appends landing AT the floor (finding D). Quiesced migration from the ADR-0011 layout preserves seqs/payloads and seals each migrated stream — the seal is the tail-erasure witness. Rejected: the ADR-0011 single-lineage event stream (all repos serialize through one head CAS, O(history) replay, lineage-wide damage); unfenced trim (unblocked only by 0001's versioned values); mode-A/mode-B fencing designs (reserved, not shipped); per-event tombstones; and for the crate itself, delivery/push/bus, forge types, and name registries — pull-only, opaque ids, the application maps names at its boundary. Flips if: retention needs grow past certified trim (a future fenced-retirement decision) or 0001's era model is superseded.\n" ;
		<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/timestamp> "2026-08-21T10:51:16" ;
		bedrock:document bedrock:path\/situation\/record\/decision-0002-streams.yamlld .
	<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/vertex/decision-0003-streaming-value-io> a <https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/ontology/Decision> ;
		<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/label> "ADR 0003: streaming-value I/O for AtomicKeyspace (superseded)" ;
		<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/references> <https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/vertex/invariant-kernel-extension> ;
		<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/statement> "The proposed v1 design for streaming large values through AtomicKeyspace: two representations behind one logical value API — inline v2 envelope up to 16 MiB; larger values as a v3 manifest in the key object plus immutable fixed-size SHA-256-addressed chunks in a kernel-private root; the manifest's conditional PUT the only commit point; readers always fetch and validate the control object first. Status at birth: PROPOSED / DRAFT — documentation only, no implementation authorized. Adjudication did not amend in place: the independent adversarial review (SHIP WITH AMENDMENTS) moved to a successor record. Superseded by ADR 0004 (decision-0004-streaming-value-io-v2), which kept the manifest/chunk architecture and amended it — this vertex is chain history, not live law; read the successor for what stands.\n" ;
		<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/timestamp> "2026-08-22T20:43:22" ;
		bedrock:document bedrock:path\/situation\/record\/decision-0003-streaming-value-io.yamlld .
	<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/vertex/decision-0004-streaming-value-io-v2> a <https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/ontology/Decision> ;
		<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/label> "ADR 0004: streaming-value I/O v2 — manifest commit, bounded chunks" ;
		<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/references> <https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/vertex/invariant-13-state> , <https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/vertex/invariant-kernel-extension> ;
		<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/requires> <https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/vertex/decision-0001-atomic-keyspace> ;
		<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/statement> "Accepted 2026-08-22 via human-delegated synthesis (\"adopt the best solution derivable from both reviewers; reserve only physics-class forks for me\"). Supersedes ADR 0003, keeping its manifest/chunk architecture under ten review amendments (SHIP WITH AMENDMENTS -> SHIP, 10/10 fidelity, evidence verified). Synthesis-adopted rulings: (1) representation = manifest/chunks — the live Exoscale probe (run 32592980637, PARTIAL MULTIPART WITNESS) proved conditional completion works but part-addressed reads are measured absent, so the portable-correctness floor stands and any backend fast path is a future, capability-probed, feature-flagged addition; (2) CHUNK_BYTES = 16 MiB, INLINE_MAX = 64 MiB, chunk_count >= 2, 2x key-encoding bound, 892 B max key, and a 16 MiB encoded streams-envelope bound so streams-stay-inline is structural; (3) chunk GC is quiesced-only v1 with a cheap fence at a kernel-reserved key, the broken-quiescence data-loss race documented and demonstrated in the rig, and delete-free online orphan metering — quiescence is an operational assertion the kernel cannot prove; (4) per-key chunk scoping, global refcounted dedup rejected; (5) 64 MiB adapter guard on git whole-read paths, with object_exists()/FindHeader::try_header() as mandatory downstream migration sites; (6) key-late writes use a bounded ephemeral spool under the same guard, durable prepared-upload rejected. Hard edges: reserved-root guard rejects lineages naming keyspace or keyspace-chunks; stale-era eviction is conditional, never read-check-unconditional; the third lost-response outcome is Unavailable/ambiguous, never a fabricated conflict. Proof plan: A24-A35 on loopback + real-S3 legs. Rejected: native multipart at the logical key (no portable part reads), mutable LIST-discovered chunks (no atomic multi-object replacement; reopens ABA per chunk), temp-object + conditional copy (double bandwidth), global content-addressed dedup (crash-safe refcounting). Flip condition: a full witness of portable part-addressed/integrity reads would remove the manifest design's largest permanent liability (chunk GC) and reopen manifest-vs-native-multipart for a human ruling.\n" ;
		<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/supersedes> <https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/vertex/decision-0003-streaming-value-io> ;
		<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/timestamp> "2026-08-22T20:43:22" ;
		bedrock:document bedrock:path\/situation\/record\/decision-0004-streaming-value-io-v2.yamlld .
	<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/vertex/decision-0005-batched-deletion> a <https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/ontology/Decision> ;
		<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/consumes> <https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/path/situation/plan/batched-deletion-primitive.yamlld> ;
		<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/label> "ADR 0005: unconditional S3 multi-object deletion — typed outcomes, bounded chunks" ;
		<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/references> <https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/vertex/decision-0004-streaming-value-io-v2> , <https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/vertex/invariant-kernel-extension> , <https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/vertex/structure-kernel> ;
		<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/requires> <https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/vertex/decision-0001-atomic-keyspace> ;
		<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/statement> "Accepted 2026-08-23 by human merge of PR #33 (merge commit 60cb5c35) after a two-round independent adversarial review — both rounds returned AMEND (round two: G1-G5 plus five nitpicks) and landed as forward commits on the proposal branch; the final re-check at witness tip b3c13365 raised zero blocking findings. Chosen: additive AtomicKeyspace::delete_objects over S3 DeleteObjects beside the published delete_many — neither wraps the other; delete_many stays frozen (A6/G117) and not deprecated, and two response-trust implementations deliberately coexist (the legacy object_store path keeps its missing-member-defaults-to- success and unrequested-key panic residuals). Transport: sequential chunks of at most 1,000 keys under DELETE_OBJECTS_MAX_INPUT = 100_000, verbose responses only, exact per-chunk response bijection — no omitted key ever defaults to success; batch is transport, never transaction, and cross-key atomicity is a permanent non-goal. No batched conditional delete: delete_if_match remains the only conditional surface, per-key, permanently. Outcomes: one typed result per input key — Ok, Rejected, Unconfirmed, NotAttempted, Unsupported — behind an admission-only outer error; an Unconfirmed stop labels its untouched tail NotAttempted, a definitive mid-call refusal labels current chunk and tail Unsupported, and remaining() is checkpoint serialization, never retry policy. The primitive sits below lifecycle machinery: no tombstone, no incarnation bump, no fence read; its fence-blindness couples to ADR 0004 quiescence as the named residual — raw batch delete plus same-incarnation/version-0 recreate can re-materialize the exact chunk paths a concurrent sweep classified as orphaned, producing ADR 0004's forbidden ManifestIncomplete (witnessed as KeyspaceError::ChunkMissing; up to 1,000 controls per request). Claims A36-A45; a real-S3 DeleteObjects leg gates publication; implementation is one separately authorized kernel-extension batch targeting the next free 0.4.x. Rejected: mutating delete_many in place, wrapping delete_many over the new method, object_store::delete_stream for the assured path, one top-level wholesale error, read-then-delete, rollback/compensation (permanent). Flips if: a portable standards-level multi-object conditional (a per-object If-Match equivalent) emerges — that demands a superseding ADR with backend qualification, never a silent extension; cross-key transactionality stays out regardless.\n" ;
		<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/timestamp> "2026-08-23T22:27:03" ;
		bedrock:document bedrock:path\/situation\/record\/decision-0005-batched-deletion.yamlld .
}

		<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/layer> "floor" ;
		<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/statement> "The dependency boundary is the assurance boundary. What crosses it version-pinned is assured-by-default at that pin; you verify your *consumption*, never the dependency's internals — the same law root already held for adopted protocols (S3, Matrix, Git), generalized to every crate boundary. Pins are assured versions; bumps are deliberate acts. A missing capability at a consumed boundary is BLOCKING — stop and escalate; working around a boundary is the disqualifying failure.\n" ;
		bedrock:document bedrock:path\/situation\/definition\/invariant-08-dependency-boundary.yamlld .
	<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/vertex/invariant-09-public-first> a <https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/ontology/Invariant> ;

		<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/layer> "floor" ;
		<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/statement> "Public-first. Before building inside, ask why this cannot be a public crate or repo; work backwards from that. Extract when the rubric passes; private only for named domain knowledge or secrets.\n" ;

		<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/statement> "One fixed toolchain per repo, canonical task names; never invent a second one.\n" ;
		bedrock:document bedrock:path\/situation\/definition\/invariant-12-toolchain.yamlld .
	<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/vertex/invariant-13-state> a <https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/ontology/Invariant> ;
		<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/label> "State: one storage truth through the kernel" ;
		<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/layer> "floor" ;
		<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/statement> "State: one storage truth through the kernel; records are immutable, created by conditional write; pointers move by CAS; every projection is rebuildable from records; reads are fenced; an integrity failure is never translated to absence.\n" ;
		bedrock:document bedrock:path\/situation\/definition\/invariant-13-state.yamlld .
	<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/vertex/invariant-14-tailscale-first> a <https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/ontology/Invariant> ;
		<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/label> "Tailscale-first" ;
		<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/layer> "floor" ;
		<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/statement> "Tailscale-first: all internal reach rides the tailnet; SSH-over-Tailscale for operators; nothing internal is served outside it; public-IP access is break-glass only.\n" ;
		bedrock:document bedrock:path\/situation\/definition\/invariant-14-tailscale-first.yamlld .
	<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/vertex/invariant-15-decisions-append-only> a <https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/ontology/Invariant> ;
		<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/label> "Decisions are append-only" ;
		<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/layer> "floor" ;
		<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/statement> "Decisions are append-only: ADRs are immutable — supersede, never edit.\n" ;
		bedrock:document bedrock:path\/situation\/definition\/invariant-15-decisions-append-only.yamlld .
	<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/vertex/invariant-16-agents-md-register> a <https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/ontology/Invariant> ;
		<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/label> "AGENTS.md is the register" ;
		<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/layer> "floor" ;
		<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/statement> "AGENTS.md is the register: one screen of numbered invariants + \"where things live\" (graph epoch: generated from `situation/`, never hand-edited). After work that changes reality, re-situate it — emit knowledge, never rules.\n" ;
		bedrock:document bedrock:path\/situation\/definition\/invariant-16-agents-md-register.yamlld .
	<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/vertex/invariant-kernel-extension> a <https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/ontology/Invariant> ;
		<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/label> "Kernel extension is human-gated" ;
		<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/layer> "situated" ;
		<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/references> <https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/vertex/decision-0001-atomic-keyspace> ;
		<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/statement> "A kernel change ships as ONE tightly scoped batch — the change, its contract suite, its proof — nothing else. Dispatches that touch the kernel state their human authorization explicitly and where the decision lives. Downstream breakage breaks definitively; repairs are separately orchestrated afterward. Do not bump the assured dependency pins casually (root Cargo.toml) — the kernel is assured at those versions.\n" ;
		bedrock:document bedrock:path\/situation\/definition\/invariant-kernel-extension.yamlld .
	<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/vertex/invariant-temp-work> a <https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/ontology/Invariant> ;
		<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/label> "Temp work lives under /Volumes/code/temp" ;
		<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/layer> "situated" ;
		<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/statement> "All scratch and temporary work lives under /Volumes/code/temp/ — nowhere else. Never mktemp, /tmp, /private/tmp, $TMPDIR, or any path on the boot drive (it is small and not ours to consume); git worktrees only in the sanctioned worktree locations; tools that default to a temp location get TMPDIR overridden or explicit output paths. When the task completes, remove what you created — leftover scratch is an incomplete delivery.\n" ;
		bedrock:document bedrock:path\/situation\/definition\/invariant-temp-work.yamlld .
}

graph:definition {
	<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/vertex/term-promise-witness-oracle> a <https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/ontology/Term> ;
		<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/label> "promise, oracle, witness, residual" ;
		<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/layer> "floor" ;
		<https://yeetz.dev/bedrock/statement> "A promise states behavior; an oracle judges promise against actual. A witness is the retained observation of one run and proves existence, never exclusivity. Residual is what was deliberately not assured, declared so everyone sees the line of demarcation — we assure the positive space only; the negative space is infinite.\n" ;
		bedrock:document bedrock:path\/situation\/definition\/term-promise-witness-oracle.yamlld .
}
